resources.string: Keep One UI. Smooth only the moment you fold.
Darken and blur only the folding region
Uses only the live system blur. Stronger on the right of the cover and on the outer edge of the inner left half. Nothing is captured.

Takes one in-memory snapshot when motion starts, recedes it in perspective over black, and adds gradient blur. Driven by measured gyro rotation. The lock screen is captured with protected content excluded; if blocked, a black perspective mask is used instead. Snapshots are never saved or uploaded.

The screen stays flat. As you fold, the region folding away, the right of the cover and the outer left of the inner display, darkens with a black gradient and is blurred throughout. No capture, so no lock-screen limits. Proportional to gyro rotation; still experimental and unverified on device.
Changing the mode restarts the engine. The effect dissolves after 1.5 s without motion and also works on the lock screen.

The pairing code input and the running status are shown as notifications. There are no ads or marketing notifications.
Go to About phone → Software information and tap Build number seven times. When you come back here it is checked automatically.
Connect to Wi-Fi first, then turn on the Wireless debugging switch in Developer options. The button opens that screen with the switch highlighted. This app cannot flip the switch for you.

In the Wireless debugging screen, open “Pair device with pairing code”. Keep that dialog open, pull down the notification shade and type only the 6-digit code into the Fold Transition notification; the port is detected automatically. Done once, the key is reused.

Used for two things: the code input field inside the pairing notification, so you can type the 6-digit code without closing the Settings dialog, and the running-status notification with a Turn off button. Optional: you can enter the port and code manually instead and turn the effect off from the app.
Wireless debugging lives only inside Developer options, so it has to be enabled once. The app reads its on/off state and changes nothing else there.

This is how the app gets the shell-level access needed to draw on the system compositor: it connects to this phone’s own ADB over loopback (127.0.0.1) and never to any other device. Wi-Fi is required only because Android starts wireless debugging exclusively on a Wi-Fi network; no internet is used. The fold effect itself needs no network at all.

Android 11 and later requires every ADB client, including this app, to be paired once before it may connect; there is no way around it without root. The app finds the pairing port automatically, so only the 6-digit code is needed. The key is stored encrypted and reused, so this is a one-time step unless you clear app data or revoke debugging authorizations.
Skip, I’ll enter the code manually
V2 perspective plane with the V3 shade

Takes the V2 in-memory snapshot and recedes it in perspective, but instead of V2’s linear gradient it lays the V3 shade on top: the folding-away side darkens with a much wider, darker black gradient than V3 and is blurred to match. Same onset, capture rules and release timing as V2. Experimental.

Fold Transition is an experimental project. It runs on Galaxy Z Fold7 and Fold8 (verified only on Fold7 SM-F966N), relies on private Samsung APIs that can change with any update, and estimates hinge motion from a gyroscope because the public sensor reports only three angles. The quality of the effect cannot be guaranteed. Nothing is uploaded and no screen content is stored.
To Samsung and other device makers

If you work on these devices: please give designers and engineers more authority over how the device feels, and please open up the hinge angle data. A public, continuous hinge angle with low latency would let third-party developers build fold transitions that are accurate instead of estimated.
Model, Android version, status and the last engine lines. No screen content.
Snapshot slides outward under the shade

Layers, top to bottom: gradient blur, black gradient shade, and the in-memory snapshot. Instead of receding in perspective, the snapshot stretches horizontally with rotation, up to 25% wider: on the cover it stretches to the right with the left edge pinned, on the inner display the left half stretches to the left with the hinge edge pinned. Same onset, capture rules and release timing as V2. Experimental.
